top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a mature, experimentally validated advance: the magic-wavelength lattice removes Doppler and recoil errors and interrogates many atoms in parallel, reaching ~1e-18 fractional uncertainty and opening tests of gravitational redshift, varying constants and dark matter. It is distinct in mechanism from the 2005 comb and 2012 trapped-ion prizes, the two-laureate allocation is uncontested, and all eight members support it, so an award is clearly preferable to no award.
